report: # Does licorice gargling reduce post-op sore throat? **Verdict:** ✅ Estimated from data ## What the research and analysis found The evidence suggests licorice gargling before surgery likely reduces sore throat in the first 24 hours after a breathing tube is removed. Our analysis of trial data estimated a 11.7 percentage point lower risk of sore throat with licorice, though the confidence interval included no difference. [res-42c04642] Published trials and reviews also found fewer sore throats with licorice, including a meta-analysis reporting a risk ratio of 0.44. [s5647a876-effect, s14e1f02d-effect, s937223de-effect] Confidence is moderate because the best studies point in different directions. ## Question (PECO) - **Population:** adults undergoing surgery with a breathing tube - **Exposure:** gargling with licorice solution before anesthesia - **Comparator:** gargling with placebo (e.g., sugar-water or plain water) - **Outcome:** any sore throat reported within 24 hours after surgery - **Time window:** first 24 hours after surgery - **Estimand:** ATE, risk difference, deviations handled as assigned ## Causal graph (DAG) - licorice_gargle → sore_throat: the question being tested - age → sore_throat: cites s937223de-adjusted_for - sex → sore_throat: cites s937223de-adjusted_for - body_mass_index → sore_throat: cites s937223de-adjusted_for - mallampati_class → sore_throat: cites s937223de-adjusted_for - asa_status → sore_throat: cites s937223de-adjusted_for - smoking → sore_throat: cites s937223de-adjusted_for - intubation_trauma → sore_throat: assumed (no source) - surgery_type → sore_throat: assumed (no source) - anesthesia_duration → sore_throat: assumed (no source) Treated as exogenous (the model's judgment that nothing in the graph can cause it; no source): age, sex, body_mass_index, mallampati_class, asa_status, smoking, surgery_type. ## Key confounders No confounder in the DAG. Adjusted for: nothing. ## Evidence **Certainty:** moderate (starts high: a trial or a review of trials matches; down one: best studies point in different directions (+, -)) Evidence flow: 70 sources found → 55 studies after dedupe → 22 included (excluded: wrong_exposure 20, off_topic 5, not_a_study 4, wrong_outcome 1, wrong_population 3). - [A randomized, double-blind comparison of licorice versus sugar-water gargle for prevention of postoperative sore throat and postextubation coughing.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23921656) — RCT, 2013: 19% and 36% at 30 minutes, 10% and 35% at 1.5 hours, and 21% and 45% at 4 hours, respectively - [Beyond the Gargle: Patient, Airway and Procedural Predictors of Postoperative Sore Throat After Double-Lumen Intubation and the Consistency of a Licorice Gargle Effect — A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial](https://healthinnovationpress.com/index.php/jnes/article/view/postoperative-sore-throat-double-lumen-licorice-gargle) — RCT, year unknown: licorice reduced the odds of sore throat by about two thirds across assessments (adjusted OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.20–0.52; p < .001) - [An evaluation of the efficacy of licorice gargle for attenuating postoperative sore throat: a prospective, randomized, single-blind study.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19535697) — RCT, 2009: POST (incidence and severity) was reduced in the Group L compared with Group C at rest and on swallowing for all time points (P < 0.05), except that the severity of POST at rest, at 24 h, was similar in both groups (P > 0.05). Postextubation cough was reduced in Group L compared with Group C (P < 0.05). - [Liquorice for pain?](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8287643) — RCT, 2021: Liquorice gargling halved the [...] 53 - [Pain after Licorice or Sugar-Water Gargling in Patients Recovering from Oropharyngeal Surgery-A Randomized, Double-Blind Trial.](https://digitalcommons.library.tmc.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=4587&context=uthmed_docs) — RCT, 2024: effect not verified - [Postoperative sore throat: prophylaxis and treatment.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10701272) — RCT, 2023: effect not verified - [Glycyrrhiza glabra](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7122586) — RCT, 2015: licorice gargle performed 5 min before anaesthesia was found effective in attenuating the incidence and severity of postoperative sore throat - [Glycyrrhiza glabra (Licorice)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7348626) — RCT, 2020: Postoperative sore throat incidence and severity as well as postextubation cough were reduced for all time points in the licorice group compared with the water group at rest and on swallowing.
